licensed_claims: shared local seasonal exposure does not guarantee matched partner temperature sensitivity

sources.citation: Climate change intensifies plant-pollinator mismatch and increases secondary extinction risk for plants in northern latitudes, PNAS 2025
licensed_claims: phenological window duration is a plausible local interaction buffer
plant-pollinator systems cannot be assumed to have negligible temporal recourse
prohibited_claims: flowering duration is equivalent to migratory speed or stopover recourse
the study estimates recourse fraction r on the PAYOFF-B binary scale
longer flowering duration always evolves or plastically changes in response to mismatch

cross_system_ceiling.supported: migration systems directly demonstrate post-commitment timing recourse and en-route cue updating; local plant-butterfly interactions directly demonstrate unequal phenological sensitivity despite shared regional environmental exposure; local interaction systems can also possess temporal-window buffering, so recourse must be measured rather than assigned by taxon
not_supported: migrants universally have greater recourse than pollinators
a pooled migrant-versus-pollinator q or r coefficient
plants or pollinators can be assigned uniformly low recourse from taxon identity alone
direct biological interpretation of reduced-form r as a physical percentage of route, stopover or flowering-duration capacity without an external mapping
cross_system_ceiling.prospective_prediction: mismatch risk should be greatest when useful pre-commitment information is weak and remaining post-commitment recourse is narrow
